part.name: Cross-strut clamp assembly
part.description: Three-solid mechanical part/assembly consisting of a long vertical strut, a long diagonal strut, and a central clamp block that captures/locates both struts and provides a through-bolt interface (with counterbores) for tightening.
part.symmetry_note: Central clamp block is largely symmetric about X=0 and Z=0 planes; overall part is not fully symmetric due to asymmetric end-hole/feature pattern on the diagonal strut.

Section.name: Vertical strut
features included: Long prismatic/rounded strut body (lengthwise along global Z)
Axial end hole/bore segments from both ends toward the center
Small transverse pin/bolt holes near clamp zone (two)
Central relief/notch surfaces and blends around the clamp engagement region
Section.function intent: Acts as the primary vertical member of the frame, providing a stiff load path and a locating datum for the central clamp/joint.
Section.physical behavior: Carries axial tension/compression and bending; the long outer skin resists bending while the end bores/lightening features reduce mass and provide an interface for fasteners or end fittings. The transverse holes provide secondary retention/anti-slip or indexing near the joint.
Section.geometry: Elongated member with a 12.7 mm thickness in Y; outer boundary is largely rounded/constant-section with end caps at Z=±190.5. Contains a coaxial axial bore (R≈3.175) broken into two segments (interrupted by the joint region). Includes transverse small holes (R≈3.175) at Z≈±25.4 and local internal planar relief at Y=6.35 around the joint cutout.
Section.location: Centered about X=0, extends predominantly in ±Z direction (largest span in Z).

Section.name: Central clamp block
features included: Main clamp body with stepped outer envelope
Through-bolt hole through thickness (axis ~Y) with counterbores
Multiple stepped planar faces providing clamping landings
Outer corner rounds/fillets (cylindrical corner patches)
Two additional small through-holes/fastener holes near the joint region
Section.function intent: Joins and locates the two struts at the crossing, constraining relative motion and enabling clamping force via a through-bolt to resist slip and transmit loads between members.
Section.physical behavior: Acts as a load-transfer node: compressive clamping force generated by a bolt creates frictional resistance and geometric constraint to prevent strut movement. The stepped geometry distributes contact pressure; rounded corners reduce stress concentration; counterbores seat fastener heads/nuts and prevent interference.
Section.geometry: Blocky stepped clamp (solid 2) centered at the origin with overall envelope approx X/Z=±25.4 and Y=-15.24..27.94. Contains a central through cylindrical hole (R≈6.35) along Y with counterbore regions (R≈9.525) on each side, plus additional internal cylindrical clearances (R≈6.477). Outer envelope formed by multiple planes (top/bottom/side) and numerous cylindrical corner fillets (R≈7.62).
Section.location: At the intersection of the vertical and diagonal struts; spans the largest thickness in Y compared to the struts.
